## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Define the tutorial packaging format

## Description

Delivers the definition of the tutorial packaging format — the metadata, pinned images,
and validation manifest that make a tutorial a versioned, independently testable
package. The format is the shared contract between the platform and tutorial content:
the tutorial gallery's launch mechanics reads it, and every authored tutorial is
packaged in it. Defining it first lets the gallery implementation and the tutorial
authoring proceed in parallel against a stable contract.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial package metadata: identity, description, the journey it covers,
  and its launch kind (open a workbench with the notebook, or import the pipeline)
- Define how a tutorial pins the images it runs on, so a tutorial executes against
  known, fixed images rather than whatever the cluster currently serves
- Define the validation manifest: the mechanism by which a tutorial's expected behavior
  is described so the tutorial can be tested against a release
- Define the versioning scheme for tutorial packages so tutorials are versioned and
  testable independently of Dashboard releases
- Publish the format as the agreed contract for the gallery implementation and for
  tutorial authors

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format is documented and covers package metadata, image pinning, and
  the validation manifest
- A tutorial package conforming to the format carries a version independent of the
  Dashboard release cadence
- A conforming tutorial package can be validated via its manifest against the current
  release without a Dashboard release
- The format definition is accepted by the teams that build against it (the gallery
  implementation and the tutorial authoring teams)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): a tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of
  Dashboard releases. The epic is scheduled at P0 by priority inheritance — it gates
  the tutorial gallery and all tutorial authoring.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch

## Description

Delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, browsable gallery of
tutorials that a user can launch into their own project with one click. Launching a
notebook tutorial opens a workbench preloaded with the tutorial notebook; launching a
pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline into the project. This is the product-code work
stream of the tutorial gallery strategy.

## Scope

- A gallery surface in the Dashboard that lists the available tutorial packages,
  reading their packaging-format metadata
- One-click launch of a notebook tutorial into the user's own project: a workbench
  created with the tutorial notebook, using the image pinned by the tutorial package
- One-click launch of a pipeline tutorial into the user's own project: the pipeline
  imported into the project
- The gallery operates within the user's existing project context, project-scoped like
  the Dashboard's other resources

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Dashboard displays a tutorial gallery listing the available tutorial packages
  with their metadata
- Launching a notebook-type tutorial from the gallery creates a workbench in the
  user's project containing the tutorial notebook, running the image pinned by the
  package
- Launching a pipeline-type tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into the
  user's project
- Both launch kinds work from a single user interaction after selecting a tutorial
- A user with an empty project reaches a running tutorial entirely through the gallery

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a
  tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the
  pipeline)

# Document the tutorial gallery and contribution process

## Description

Delivers the documentation for the tutorial gallery: end-user documentation for using
the gallery, and documentation of the contribution process for new tutorials. This is
the documentation work stream; it is authored after the packaging format, the gallery,
and the tutorials exist so the docs describe what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline:
- Using the gallery: browsing the available tutorials and launching one into your
  project, for both launch kinds (workbench with the notebook, pipeline import)
- Contributing a new tutorial: the contribution process — authoring, packaging per the
  tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), and
  validation — documented as a process only; no submission tooling this release (out of
  scope per the strategy)
- Placement of both topics in the product documentation set

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers using the tutorial gallery: browsing tutorials and launching
  them into a project, for both launch kinds
- Documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials, including how a
  tutorial is packaged and validated per the packaging format
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and
  tutorial set

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for
  new tutorials

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019: Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

The strategy delivers a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: maintained, tested
tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch into their own project with
one click. The problem statement itself identifies three kinds of work with different
owners and review processes — product code (the gallery and launch mechanics), authored
content (the tutorials), and documentation — so the decomposition follows those
work-stream boundaries, plus the packaging format that decouples content from
Dashboard releases.

graph TD

| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The gallery's launch mechanics parses the packaging format's metadata and pinned images — Dashboard code building against a contract another epic produces. |
